inputs.name: neural_map
inputs.meaning: student map: cell [i, j] = (x_i, y_j, z_ij, u_ij) in the yaw-aligned base frame; i = x index (outer, 29, -0.42..1.26 m), j = y index (inner, 13, -0.36..0.36 m); z = fused height - base z + 0.27 clipped to [-1.5, 1.5]; u = 0.5 * ln(clip(variance, 0.01, 2)) + 0.5

inputs.name: prop_hist
inputs.meaning: 20 rows, oldest first, one row per policy step: base_ang_vel 3 | projected_gravity 3 | joint_pos - default 12 | joint_vel 12 | last raw action clipped to +-50 12; body frame, scale 1; after a reset the first row fills all 20 rows; no privileged term (no base_lin_vel)

inputs.name: cmds
inputs.meaning: goal [x, y, sin(e), cos(e)], see command

outputs.name: actions
outputs.meaning: a: deterministic mean of the actor (raw, before scale and offset), Isaac joint order

outputs.name: attn_out
outputs.meaning: diagnostic: attention output (the latent matched to the teacher in training)

outputs.name: global_feat
outputs.meaning: diagnostic: global context of the map

actor_input_order.note: an object, not the array of the teacher bundles: do not reuse a reader written for the teacher contract; go by the correspondence below

prop_hist_row.formula: clip(a_prev, -50, 50), a_prev = the raw action actually ADOPTED before this step (a late output that was discarded is not stored, the previously adopted one is kept), 0 after a reset

actor_input_order.history: rows oldest first; one append per policy step; the first append after a reset fills all 20 rows

map_input_order: first input 'neural_map' (agent obs_groups.actor = [neural_map, student_prop_hist, student_cmds], agent.yaml:7-11; the ONNX takes them by name)

command.frame: goal position relative to the base, rotated by the base yaw only (x forward, y left)
command.far_goal_rule: if |(x, y)| > 2.0 m (strictly above): (x, y) scaled to norm 2.0 and e replaced by ONE uniform draw in [-pi, pi) of this policy step, whose sin and cos are fed; at exactly 2.0 m nothing is scaled and the real e is kept. Beyond 2 m the bearing of the goal POSITION stays valid (3 m ahead becomes 2 m ahead); only the yaw-error sin / cos is replaced
command.remote_control_mapping: none: no formula from the remote control axes to this command exists (CONTRACT.md 3.5, 7a)
command.real_robot_needs: base position and yaw in a world frame (localisation); training used the simulator's true pose

state_note: no recurrent state in either ONNX (state_feedback false). The caller keeps: the 20-row history, the previous raw action, the fused map

action.formula: target_q = default_joint_pos + 0.25 * actions (Isaac order); target velocity 0; feed-forward torque 0
outside_onnx: keep a_prev = actions (raw) ONLY when this output was adopted as the joint target; if it was discarded as late, a_prev stays the previously adopted one; next row[30:42] = clip(a_prev, -50, 50)
action.last_action_obs: raw action before scale / offset / delay, clipped to +-50
action.team_runner_note: the team's low-level runner clips the target to default +- 1.6 rad, which training did not have (CONTRACT.md 7b)

motor_model.class: Go2HVActuator (the simulation motor model of training, as in the bundle ame2-m30001)
motor_model.pd: tau = kp * (target_q - q) + kd * (0 - dq), evaluated every physics step (200 Hz)

control_note: 0.005 s x 4 = 0.020 s per policy step, its reciprocal 50 Hz

action_delay.sampled: once per episode at reset, per robot
action_delay.applied: FIFO over physics steps (4 per control step)
action_delay.note: the delay range put into training; not a record of passing at every delay

map.alignment: yaw (grid rotated by the base yaw only)
map.origin: base position (x, y, z) of the same policy step
map.source: the fused map of the mapper pipeline (see mapper), NOT a ground-truth scan
map.z_definition: z = fused height (world) - base z (world) + 0.27, clipped to [-1.5, 1.5]
map.u_definition: u = 0.5 * ln(clip(variance, 0.01, 2.0)) + 0.5; cells never written carry the prior (variance 10 -> u = 0.8466)
map.query: nearest fused cell of every policy cell centre at the pose of the policy step; outside the fused map: the prior and variance 10

inputs.name: grid
inputs.meaning: local grid in the base-yaw frame: max z (relative to the base, clamped to [-1.5, 1.0]) of the points of both sensors per 4 cm cell, empty cell = -3.0; [i (x, 66)][j (y, 48)]

outputs.name: elevation
outputs.meaning: height estimate per cell, relative to the base

outputs.name: logvar
outputs.meaning: log variance per cell, clipped to [-9.2, 3.0] inside the graph

local_grid.frame: base position, base yaw only; z = point z (world) - base z (world)
local_grid.sensors_merged_by: cell-wise maximum of the grids of the two sensors
local_grid.cell_index: i = round((x - x0) / 0.04), j = round((y - y0) / 0.04) on the cell CENTRES, round half to even; then the range check 0 <= i < 66, 0 <= j < 48 (points outside are dropped)

update.rule: the code makes a frame when EITHER sensor's time stamp changed and fuses the LATEST points of BOTH sensors; in the simulation both sensors refresh at the same policy step (one frame per 5 steps). With sensors that refresh separately a scan can be fused again: the pairing by sensor time and the handling of a stale pair are open (CONTRACT.md 7a); the policy map is read at every policy step

lidar.mount_grade: assumption: the URDF radar link pose, not measured on the robot

depth.mount_grade: setting + code comment: the value of env.yaml, written in a comment of patch_stu.py as the team's measurement on the real Go2; the measurement document itself was not read

sensors.invalid_points: no return, out of range, blocked by the robot's own body boxes or dropped: invalid, never filled; an update is discarded as a whole when terrain lies above the sensor origin (within 2 m)

fusion.map: world-aligned square per robot, 4.8 m, 120 x 120 cells of 0.04 m, world heights
fusion.prior: flat ground at base z - 0.27 at the reset (or at the last recentring for new cells), variance 10
fusion.rule: per world cell: its centre is moved into the base-yaw frame and the local cell index is rounded (half to even); with R = exp(logvar) of that local cell and P the stored variance, R_eff = max(R, 0.5 * P). Written only when ALL hold: (1) the index is inside the local grid, (2) the measured height (elevation + base z) is finite, (3) logvar < float32(ln 15) (at or above, or NaN: rejected), (4) R_eff < 1.5 * P or R_eff < 0.04; then with probability P / (P + R_eff): height <- elevation + base z, variance <- R_eff
fusion.reject_note: ln 15; the test lv < reject_logvar is made on float32 values, a NaN is rejected
fusion.random: the take test draws a uniform number per cell
fusion.reset: a new map at every episode reset (reset event go2_reset_neural_map)

mapper.to_policy: elevation / logvar are fused into the world map; the policy input neural_map (channels z, u) is read from that map; the mapper output is never fed to the policy directly
mapper.gaze: no gaze input: the policy computes the gaze position and its 12 x 10 window inside its ONNX
mapper.network: observed = grid > -2.95; encoder input = two channels (the height with unseen cells set to 0, the observed mask) -> 2 x Conv3x3 (32) ELU -> MaxPool 3 -> nearest upsampling -> concat skip -> 2 x Conv3x3 (32) ELU -> three 1x1 heads (raw height, gate, logvar); elevation = gate * raw + (1 - gate) * input with the ORIGINAL input (unseen cells -3.0); logvar clamped to [-9.2, 3.0]; 37,667 weights (read from the TorchScript forward code and the ONNX graph)
mapper.frames_per_call: the bundle, step 3 and the robot run one frame per call; training ran up to 512 frames per call on the GPU (a memory setting). The number of frames per call is not neutral for the output: CPU measurement in judgement_summary.json mapper_batch_size_effect; nothing measured on the training GPU

parity.note: above the threshold on the stairs recording (parity.json tags.stairs); see CONTRACT.md 7

network.history_encoder: Conv1d(42->16, k5) ELU Flatten Linear(256->64) ELU over the 20 rows
network.recent_encoder: Linear(126->60) ELU over the last 3 rows
network.global_context: Conv(4->8,k3) ELU Conv(8->32,k3,dil2) ELU -> spatial max -> Linear 32-64 ELU (whole 29x13 map, all four channels)
network.gaze: Linear(192-64) ELU Linear(64-2) -> sigmoid -> integer 12x10 crop (round, clamp)
network.crop_encoder: per cell Linear(4-16) ELU | Conv(z,u: 2->8,k5,p2) ELU Conv(8->48,k5,p2) ELU | concat 64 -> Linear 96 ELU -> 120 tokens

excluded: sensor noise, dropout, artifacts, mount jitter
points -> local grid, fusion and the policy-map query (done by the caller, see mapper)

app_onnx.note: same form as the app_onnx cell of the simulation bundles, for the real-robot runner; no separate app_onnx.json (that file belongs to the simulation bundle). Input order = ONNX session input order (measured). Of the three outputs the runner uses actions; attn_out and global_feat are diagnostic
